newsitem.title: UK: BOXING-NASEEM TO DEFEND TITLES AGAINST HARDY.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-NASEEM TO DEFEND TITLES AGAINST HARDY.

text.p: Veteran European champion Billy Hardy was named on Monday as the surprise challenger for Prince Naseem Hamed's unified featherweight world titles.

The 32-year-old Englishman will fight Naseem for the International Boxing Federation (IBF) and World Boxing Organisation (WBO) crowns in Manchester on May 3 -- the same night as the World Boxing Association (WBA) heavyweight title clash between Evander Holyfield and Mike Tyson in Las Vegas.
Naseem had been expected to face WBA featherweight champion Wilfredo Vasquez of Puerto Rico but promoter Frank Warren said that fight would have to wait until later in the year.
"In an ideal world I would have preferred Naseem to fight Vasquez or (World Boxing Council featherweight champion) Luisito Espinosa but unfortunately it's not to be," Warren told a news conference.
"Hopefully he'll be fighting one of those guys in June or July."
Naseem, a renowned showman who somersaults into the ring before fights, dismissed Hardy as "just a little stepping stone towards me uniting all the belts and bringing them all back to England".
"Billy comes to the table with zilch (nothing). He just comes with his bag. Do I want to dodge Billy Hardy? You must be joking."
Hardy described himself as "King Billy" and vowed to dethrone the prince.
Naseem has won all his previous 25 fights and said he would stop Hardy within five rounds.
